newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela bolivar ends off as corporates buy dlrs.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela bolivar ends off as corporates buy dlrs.

text.p: The Venezuelan bolivar closed off at 484.25/485.25 per dollar in skittish trade on strong corporate dollar demand and only slight Central Bank participation, traders said.
The bolivar closed Friday at 483.75/484.75 per dollar.
"There was a lot of demand, which the Central Bank only met partially and that drove down the exchange rate," said one trader.

Venezuela's foreign exchange market is unusual in that the Central Bank is its largest single supplier of dollars, which blurs the difference between the Central Bank supplying liquidity and intervening.
Traders said buyers continued to feel nervous on lingering fears of an accelerated rate of depreciation for the bolivar.
The rumors were firmly denied last week by both Central Bank president Antonio Casas Gonzalez and Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar.
